camera.note: lod/BLOCK-L.md, measured: at the 315 deg bearing proj() is axis-aligned, so a world metre is pxAcross * cam.scale px across the screen and pxDown * cam.scale down it. z = cam.scale / cam.base.

terrain.note: One byte a node, 0..255 mapped over 0..zmax metres. `mask` is one bit a node, 1 = land. Both are the mock's own arrays, byte-identical.

coast.note: World metres, f32. Ring lengths are VERTEX counts, not byte counts.

blocks.note: Per block: a ring origin (ox, oy) in world metres and `cnt` vertices as i16 deltas at scale `sc` (a per-block power-of-two quantiser). `z` is the ring's ground elevation, `a` its published area in m2, `hood` an index into hoodNames. Block IDs are strings and live in blocks-id.json, because nothing in the draw path needs them. `bidx` is the block's measured roof colour as an index into the SAME 32-entry palette the buildings use — manifest.buildings.palette, dark to light — so one table tones both tiers and the batch key survives. 255 is the NOBLOCK sentinel: no sampled building stood on that block (park, water, right of way), 361 of 5,404, and the renderer must fall back rather than index the palette with it.

massing.note: `ty` is year - year0. `tc` is coverage x 255. `th` is mean height in metres. `solo` is one bit per building over LODM.n: 1 = drawn as itself at every zoom (outside every assessor block, or tall enough that folding it into a mean would delete the skyline).

bldg.note: The 15,261 SOLOS — drawn as themselves at every zoom, and excluded from their block's coverage and mean so nothing is counted twice. They are NOT repeated in any bldg cell.

face.note:
Per building, in this cell's own order, matching bldg/<same id>.qc gid for gid. `role` is one entry per RING VERTEX (the edge leaving it).
THE STOREY SUPPLEMENT (st2): bldg/ingest.py read the footprint file's `mblr` as mblr[2:9], a fixed seven-character slice, and the storey count inherited it. But wv5m-vpq2's parcel_number is SEVEN, EIGHT OR NINE characters (176,031 / 32,003 / 3,513 roll rows), so the slice truncated every parcel on an assessor block with a letter suffix: block 0460A lot 001 is published as 0460A001 and the slice asked for 0460A00, which matches nothing. The slice resolved 149,445 footprints (89.9 %); the whole mblr resolves 159,852 (96.2 %). The truncation was fixed at source on 2026-08-23, so `st` in the bldg chunk already holds every value this array carries. It is kept because the two were derived from SEPARATE downloads by separate lookups and they agree on 9,984 of 9,984 element for element — which is the evidence that the fix recovered published data rather than invented it. Read `st` first; this never decides anything.

water.note: Level 0: every 4th node of the shipped grid, which IS the published coarse grid the 4x refinement was built from. Not a resampling and lossless with respect to that grid. Depth in metres = (v/255)^2 * dmax.

surround.note: Cell (i,j) is at k = j*w + i, j increasing NORTH. Elevation in metres = dem[k]/255*zmax. `land` and `own` are one bit a cell, MSB first within each byte (numpy packbits), so bit k is (a[k>>3] >> (7-(k&7))) & 1. `land` is the hydrography's own land bit and is what the shoal band's BFS measures distance from. `own` is `land` AND NOT already drawn by the city model — gen_context.py dilates the city's 260x260 mask by two cells and subtracts it, so the two shorelines cannot disagree into a fringe of the wrong tone. ONLY `own` CELLS ARE PAINTED: drawSurround walks `order` and applies no land test of its own, so `order` must be built over `own`. `segs` is 4 NODE indices a segment (i0,j0,i1,j1) for the surround's own fainter shoreline. Node (i,j) is at world x = world[0] + i*cellW, y = world[1] + j*cellH, with w+1 by h+1 nodes. THE CELL IS 110.01 x 139.15 m AND THAT IS THE DIVISOR THE HILLSHADE NEEDS: buildSurroundLam takes cellW/cellH and the shipped mock divided by 1.8 instead, over-reading slope 61x across and 77x down. Nothing is hillshaded here; the field and the cell size are carried so it can be done right downstream.

hero.note: Hero q owns parts poff[q]..poff[q+1]; part j owns ring vertices roff[j]..roff[j+1] and profile points proff[j]..proff[j+1]. Every i32 field is CENTIMETRES — divide by 100 for metres — and is exact, because every authored value is a whole centimetre. `rx`/`ry`/`pu`/`ps` are f32 world metres RELATIVE TO THE ANCHOR (ax, ay). `pk` 0=solid 1=arcade 2=rib. `pc` and `pdk` are the mock decoder's RESOLVED values (c defaults to m, dk to 0.75). `ppi` = -1 means one opening and no repetition (the file writes 1e9). `acc` = -1 means the crown carries no chroma. `hull` = 1 on Sutro Tower alone and base/heroes.json says why. Names, anchors, year sources and the drawn/measured prose are in base/heroes.json, keyed by the same index.

cap.note: Cap c sits on building bi[c] and takes profile prof[c], whose points are pu/ps over poff[prof]..poff[prof+1]. `u` is height fraction in [0,1], monotone; `s` is radius scale. Profile 0 is `prism` — the identity — and no cap uses it. The profile table is shared and is the same six `render-data.js` ships.

bridge.note: `rx`/`ry` are the published deck ring, 5 vertices, closed. `tx`/`ty` are the two towers. THE YEAR IS 1937 — the NBI's completion year, which is when the bridge existed. 1933 is `rzic-39gi`'s `yearbuilt` and is when construction BEGAN; it is carried as `yearLandmark` and is NOT the gate. The main cable's low point is drawn AT the deck, so the sag is the difference between two published figures (towerHeadM - deckZ = 164.55 m) and not a number of its own. The suspender spacing (30 m) and the leg size (7 m) are drawing decisions; nothing publishes them.

strt.note: Right-of-way and roadway rings are stored ABSOLUTE in world metres (f32) rather than as the source's per-ring delta chain: a cell holds a few hundred rings, the delta chain's gzip win is a whole-file effect, and absolute coordinates make a cell independently decodable. `rdKerb` is one bit per ROADWAY vertex: is the edge leaving it a published KERB (1,961.6 km) or the outer edge of the right of way (1,768.9 km)? The far edge of a right of way is a property line and is never drawn as a kerb.

strt-misc.note: 1,120 published islands and 268 published stair runs, citywide — too few to tile. Coordinates are u16 at scale q from (ox, oy): world = ox + v*q. `cov` is one bit per right of way: does the Board's record cover it?

tree.note: Trees are keyed on the source's own 24 m grid: cellKey = row*600 + col, cell origin (-7200, -6600). `pos` is two nibbles, x and y within the cell at 1.5 m. `yr` is the planting year the register gives, 0 where it gives none — 125,234 of the trees carry no date and are drawn undated rather than dropped.

canopy.note: Canopy blobs engage at z = 1.55 (VZ_C0), before street trees at 2.90, and the whole city is still in one frame at 1.55, so this is one citywide chunk and not a tiling: 130 cells of 1.5 KB would cost more in requests than the cull saves. The ground TINT is separate — see base/canopy-tint, which is on the first-paint path because it colours the ground at every zoom.

canopy-tint.note: The canopy fraction on the DEM's own 53.8 m grid, for the ground tint. part3.html smooths it with two passes of a separable 1-2-1 kernel at load: the field is a coverage FRACTION, so smoothing it is smoothing a measurement rather than inventing one, and no cell is moved. Raw, one cell of the Presidio's forest against its neighbour of open sand is a hard 53.8 m square — the exact artefact Block M spent a night removing from the shoreline.

parks.note: Ring lengths are VERTEX counts. Coordinates are i32 DECIMETRES: world metres = v / 10.

facade.NOT_MEASURED: Where a window is. The roll counts storeys, rooms and units and does not record an opening. What is drawn inside a wall is a TYPICAL facade consistent with the published storey count, class, era and measured wall — not a survey of that building.

water.note: Node (i, j) maps to world by linear interpolation over `world`; j increases NORTH. Depth in metres = (v/255)^2 * dmax.

real: shoreline: US Census TIGERweb Areal Hydrography + county coverage (public domain)
elevation: USGS 3DEP ImageServer exportImage, float32 metres (public domain)
meta.note: The surround carries no buildings. We have no record for it, and San Francisco is the subject.

surround.note: The surround carries no buildings and no blocks: there is no record for it and San Francisco is the subject. The bathymetry in `water` is this grid refined 4x (mul=4), so every 4th node of that grid IS a node of this one.

landmarks.msAreaNote: ms.a is the area of the footprint ring AS DRAWN — the published DataSF ynuv-fyni ring after the mock's own 1 m vertex quantiser (BLDG.q = 1.0). For City Hall the published ring is 11,205.92 m2 and the quantised ring is 11,251.5 m2, +0.407 %. The gate is stated against the drawn ring, so the drawn ring's area is what this field carries; a reader quoting a footprint should quote the published figure and say which.

bridge.note: 1937 is completion and opening; 1933 is when construction began. The map draws where the bridge IS, so the gate is 1937.

landmarks.notSoloNote: These heroes' footprints are not in base/solo, so their anchors could not be read at first paint and are shipped on the hero record instead.
landmarks.note: Emphasis is a property of the DRAWING. The landmark buildings on this map are drawn at EMPHASIS, not to scale. Each one keeps its published footprint, its published position and the year a published register gives it; what is exaggerated is only how large it is drawn, by up to 5.0 times, and only while it would otherwise be too small on screen to recognise. The measured height and area are carried on every record here and are what the page states. See wonder/BLOCK-WONDER.md.

dem.what: elevation, 3DEP-derived, resampled to the piece's own 260 x 260 frame
dem.quantised: one byte a node over 0..300 m

blocks.what: 227,937 active parcels dissolved by assessor block

block_paint.publisher: Esri World Imagery (ArcGIS Online public tiles)
block_paint.what: the AREA-WEIGHTED mean of the measured roof colours of the buildings standing on the block. Area-weighted because the massing solid IS those roofs seen from far away, so a 2,000 m2 warehouse owns more of those pixels than the cottage beside it.
block_paint.measured: per building, the MEDIAN colour of the published aerial pixels inside the footprint, eroded 1.5 m inward so the sample is roof and not wall or kerb; zoom 18 = 0.472 m/px, 8,661 tiles, retrieved 2026-08-23; 166,042 of 166,166 footprints returned a sample (99.9 %)
block_paint.membership: the block whose published ring CONTAINS the footprint's centroid; 152,242 of the 166,042 sampled footprints landed on one (91.7 %). The rest are solos and made land outside the assessor grid.
block_paint.quantised: 32 palette entries, the same table the buildings use; mean error 5.8 against a median difference of 88 between two randomly chosen SF roofs
block_paint.coverage: 5,043 of 5,404 blocks carry a measured index (93.3 %); the 361 that do not are park, water or right of way and ship 255
block_paint.not_measured: the roof from above TODAY. Not the colour anyone painted the front, not a claim about roofing material, and not the colour the block was in any past year.

massing.what: cumulative built coverage and area-weighted mean LIDAR height per (assessor block, that block's own build year)
massing.membership: the block whose published ring CONTAINS the footprint's centroid; no nearest-block fallback

bldg_index.what: the building's index in bldg-data.js, which every other per-building array in this record is keyed on

bldg_h.what: hgt_mediancm, the median LIDAR return over the footprint

bldg_use.what: use_definition folded to 7 classes, plus provenance flags

roof_hf.what: the SUB-METRE residual of hgt_mediancm that the one-byte whole-metre height rounds away. Without it 36.0 % of neighbouring buildings on a block draw at exactly the same height, against 0.7 % in the published data.

paint.publisher: Esri World Imagery (ArcGIS Online public tiles)
paint.what: the median colour of the published aerial pixels inside each footprint, eroded 1.5 m inward so the sample is roof and not wall or kerb; zoom 18 = 0.472 m/px, retrieved 2026-08-23; 166,042 of 166,166 returned a sample
paint.quantised: 32 palette entries, mean error 5.8 against a median difference of 88 between two randomly chosen SF roofs
paint.not_measured: the roof from above TODAY. Not the colour anyone painted the front, not a claim about roofing material, and not the colour the building was in any past year.

fac_ty.what: property_class_code read as nine building types; 147,601 of 166,166 (88.8 %)

fac_st2.what: the storey supplement — a JOIN CORRECTION, now dead, kept as evidence. See the note.

fac_shop.what: the one bit of property_class_code that says THE GROUND FLOOR IS A SHOP (6,803)

fac_role.what: two bits per ring EDGE: does the edge face a published street centreline (162,305 buildings), and does another published footprint stand against it (163,536 of 885,776 edges)

bathymetry.what: bathymetry over gen_context.py's own frame and projection
bathymetry.quantised: sqrt to one byte a node over 0..120.0 m; worst error 0.452 m
bathymetry.licence: works of the US government, public domain

surround-hydro.what: the shoreline and the county coverage envelope that carve land from water outside San Francisco
surround-hydro.licence: US Census: 'The TIGER/Line Shapefiles ... are not copyrighted.' Work of the US government, public domain

surround-elevation.what: elevation outside the city, float32 metres, resampled to the 416 x 280 context frame and smoothed by two 1-2-1 passes (gen_context.py: a 139 m cell straddling a cliff reads as a staircase); zeroed where the hydrography says water
surround-elevation.quantised: one byte a cell over 0..420.0 m — the source file's own quantiser, 1.647 m a step, worst error 0.824 m
surround-elevation.licence: USGS: 'USGS-authored or produced data and information are in the public domain.'

hero-authoring.what: authored landmark geometry — the parts, their profiles and their materials. The FOOTPRINT, the POSITION, the YEAR and the MEASURED top and area of every hero are published and named per hero in base/heroes.json (`an`, `ys`, `ms`, `dr`); what is authored is the SHAPE carved inside them
hero-authoring.quantised: heights, cut-offs, pitches and margins in centimetres (exact — every authored value is a whole centimetre); ring and profile coordinates f32, which is the precision part3.html itself draws them at
hero-authoring.not_measured: A hero is drawn at EMPHASIS, up to 5.0x, and is therefore NOT TO SCALE. The exaggeration applies to the drawing and never to a claim: the published footprint, position and year are unchanged, and the measured top and area travel on every record. The landmark buildings on this map are drawn at EMPHASIS, not to scale. Each one keeps its published footprint, its published position and the year a published register gives it; what is exaggerated is only how large it is drawn, by up to 5.0 times, and only while it would otherwise be too small on screen to recognise. The measured height and area are carried on every record here and are what the page states. See wonder/BLOCK-WONDER.md.

bldg-footprint-centroid.what: the hero's ground anchor: the arithmetic mean of its own published footprint ring's vertices, which is part3.html's UX/UY. Derived here rather than read from the hero file because the mock derives it too, and because 3 of the 11 buildings are not solos so the ring is not at base tier

cap-shape.what: which published buildings are given a shaped cap, and which of six profiles each is given. Measured, per the source: deck line and extent: DataSF 97yj-54sx, Article 10 landmark no. 222; main span, structure length, deck width, navigational vertical clearance, year built, structure kind and type: FHWA National Bridge Inventory 2023 (California), structure 27 0052; tower position and tower height: FAA Digital Obstacle File, obstacles 06-000771 and 06-000108, type BRIDGE; second-solid height and area: DataSF ynuv-fyni zonal statistics, by form/model3.py (Block C) — unchanged here; footprint and base height: DataSF ynuv-fyni — unchanged here; place class: nc68-ngbr department_name, gtr9-ntp6 propertytype, rzic-39gi proptype, 5kya-mfst Tall Building Inventory; Transamerica Pyramid height: DataSF 5kya-mfst height_ft, corroborated by FAA DOF 06-000928 at the same figure
cap-shape.not_measured: the SHAPE of every cap — dome, spire, campanile, crown, arcade. The data fixes the top height and the plan area and says nothing about taper. Every profile is carved inside the measured solid: no ring is wider than the measured radius and none is higher than the measured top, so a drawn cap is always SMALLER than what was measured, never larger. the Golden Gate's cables, their parabolic curve and the spacing of the suspenders. The low point of the main cable is drawn at the deck, so the sag is the difference between two published figures (231.6 m tower head - 67.1 m clearance) rather than a number of its own. the taper of the Transamerica Pyramid, linear from its measured footprint to the published apex. the roof wash that marks a published class. It is a legend, not a claim about roofing material.

ggb-deck.what: Article 10 landmark no. 222, designated 1999 — the deck corridor, five vertices. Corroborated by US Census TIGERweb Primary Roads 'Golden Gate Brg': 9 of its 11 vertices fall inside this ring, and both files stop at 37.8254 N, the county line mid-channel, because that is where San Francisco stops
ggb-deck.not_measured: The deck is drawn FLAT: no deck height is published in either file, and the Bay Bridge on this map is flat for the same reason. It carries no family colour, no place mark, no hit target and no money — the corpus decision `golden-gate-bridge` has `geometry_source: NOT IN RECORD`, so nothing here may imply this line is that decision's position

ggb-nbi.what: main span 1280.2 m, structure length 2742.3 m, deck width 18.9 m, navigational vertical clearance 67.1 m, YEAR_BUILT_027 = 1937
ggb-nbi.licence: work of the US government, public domain

ggb-faa.dataset: Digital Obstacle File, obstacles 06-000771 and 06-000108, type BRIDGE
ggb-faa.what: tower position and tower height: 760 ft above sea level, 757 ft above ground. The only published file found that gives both. Positions are to the whole arc-second — 31 m of latitude here — and are projected onto the published deck line, moving them 6.64 m and 1.17 m
ggb-faa.licence: work of the US government, public domain

street_row.what: 22,191 published rights of way, as AREA

street_cls.what: classcode: 2/3 arterial, 4 collector, 5 local residential, 0 minor and private court

street_year.what: the year the Board is recorded accepting, paving and kerbing each right of way, out of the Journal of Proceedings

street_kerb.what: the published kerb; roadway = right of way minus every closed kerb ring that meets it

tree.defect: FIXED 2026-08-23, recorded because the fix is invisible in the data. world/build_world.py keyed cells as gj*GW + gi with GW = 400 columns of 24 m = 9,600 m, while the city is 14,272 m wide from that origin and needs 595. Every tree east of x = 2,376 (about Van Ness) folded 9,600 m west, so the eastern city had no trees and the western city wore them. Measured proof at the time: column 0 is open Pacific ~800 m off Ocean Beach and held 192 tree cells. GW is now 600 (14,400 m) and the grid covers the city. The canopy array shares the origin, the GW and the arithmetic and was affected and fixed identically. Kept in the manifest so nobody re-derives it: 400 buckets is 14.4 km at 36 m and 9.6 km at 24 m, and the cell size moved while this constant did not.
